This is precisely the low-S/N tail Layer 1 exists for; the ratio is large because the input was meaningless, not because the override moved a measured star.

KNOWN MISFIRE, not a legitimate snap — this is a FOREGROUND star the LMC override captured. Its DR3 parallax is 3.5695 ± 0.0105 mas (S/N 340, RUWE 0.67), placing it at 280 pc; an LMC member sits at 49.6 kpc where the parallax would be ~0.02 mas and unmeasurable, so a 340-sigma detection rules LMC membership out. The override gates on sky cone + bulk proper motion ONLY (applyLmcKinematicOverride) and has no parallax-quality test, so a nearby star that happens to lie toward the LMC and share its apparent motion is snapped 177x too far. Tracked as stellata-uadc.39; the entry stays pinned so the misfire is visible rather than silent.

simbad.reason: SIMBAD's own parallax is the noise here, not our distance: 0.2848 ± 0.8358 mas (S/N 0.34) for HD 7481, which is what its 3,511 pc inverts from. A value consistent with zero at 1/3 sigma states no distance at all. The build places the record at 258 pc from a measured tier. Pinned so a future SIMBAD refresh that publishes a real parallax for it surfaces as a change.
